name: Mount Sharp Boxwork Ridges and Hollows
finding: Observation: Curiosity imaged the 'Nevado Sajama 2' drill hole with MAHLI on Sol 4803 (2026-02-09) and planned APXS and MAHLI bedrock observations ('Mollecita', 'Monte Cielo') while driving along wide boxwork ridges and hollows; orbital HiRISE (PIA26306) observed the 10–20 km weblike ridge network on lower Mount Sharp. Interpretation: Scientists interpret the boxwork ridges as ancient groundwater-deposited minerals in bedrock fractures left standing after softer rock eroded.

source.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4804-4811: Kicking Off the Final Phase of Boxwork Exploration (with PIA26306 HiRISE context)

limitations: Exact pixel coordinates on active raster 'hirise-mro-pia26306-boxwork-2048x1042-v1' are unavailable because the blog post and PIA26306 caption do not provide pixel tie-points.
Ancient groundwater mineralization is an interpretation and does not establish current liquid water.

Direct HTTP fetch to jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-curiosity-rover-explores-a-spiderweb-on-mars/ returned HTTP 403 Forbidden; verified via accessible science.nasa.gov mission blog and PIA26306 catalog page instead.

name: Vera Rubin Ridge ('Pettegrove Point' / 'Ailsa Craig' Target)
finding: Observation: On Sol 2121 on Vera Rubin Ridge ('Pettegrove Point' member), Curiosity brushed drill target 'Ailsa Craig' with the Dust Removal Tool (DRT) and characterized it using MAHLI and APXS. Derivation: Orbital data indicated a varying hematite signal across Vera Rubin Ridge drill sites.

source.title: Curiosity Mission Update — Sol 2121: Blackjack! (Vera Rubin Ridge)

limitations: Vera Rubin Ridge is a regional Mount Sharp traverse milestone outside or unverified within the PIA26306 boxwork pixel frame; position is unavailable.
Source documents Sol 2121 MAHLI/APXS characterization and orbital hematite signal but does not state an exact Earth UTC date or quantitative mineral percentages.

name: Glen Torridon Clay-Bearing Unit to Sulfate-Rich Strata Transition
instrument: Left Navigation Camera / Drill / CheMin / SAM (Curiosity Rover)
finding: Observation: Curiosity sampled the mudstone-dominated Murray formation and clay-bearing Glen Torridon region (including drill sample #22 'Glen Etive' and drill hole #33 'Maria Gordon' near Greenheugh Pediment on Sol 3251, imaged by Left Navcam on Sol 3247), where drilled samples are delivered to CheMin and SAM. Interpretation: The ascent from clay-rich Glen Torridon rocks toward the sulfate-rich layers higher on Mount Sharp tracks a major environmental transition.

source.title: Curiosity Mission Update — Sols 3251-3253: Celebrating Another Go Around

limitations: Regional Mount Sharp stratigraphic traverse context; exact pixel coordinates on raster 'hirise-mro-pia26306-boxwork-2048x1042-v1' are unavailable.
Source summarizes multi-sol campaign milestones (Sols 236–3251) rather than single-sample quantitative chemical assay tables; does not establish route safety or slope stability.
